cases.sentence: Я бился над этой ___ три года подряд.
cases.translation: I struggled with this puzzle for three years running.
cases.explain: The preposition «над» meaning 'over, at' (working at something) always governs the instrumental: над загадкой.

cases.translation: It fills me with disgust and horror.
cases.explain: Both nouns are direct objects of «внушает», so they stand in the accusative; ужас is inanimate, so its accusative equals the nominative.

cases.sentence: Максим Горький ___ о них не споет.
cases.translation: Maxim Gorky will sing no songs about them.
cases.explain: The object of the negated verb «не споет» goes into the genitive; the plural genitive of песня is песен.

cases.translation: Better leave extragalactic astronomy to the Yankees.
cases.explain: The person you leave something TO is the indirect object, which takes the dative: оставьте янкам.

cases.translation: And we, I repeat, will occupy ourselves with hiccups.
cases.explain: The verb «заняться / заниматься» (to take up, busy oneself with) requires its object in the instrumental.

cases.translation: Let the scoundrel of an African build his Aswan dam.
cases.explain: «Плотина» is the direct object of «строит», and feminine nouns in -а take -у in the accusative.

cases.sentence: Давайте лучше займитесь икотой, то есть исследованием пьяной икоты в ее математическом ___.
cases.translation: Better take up hiccups instead, that is, the study of drunken hiccups in their mathematical aspect.
cases.explain: «В» answering «в чём?» (a state or respect, not motion into) takes the prepositional: в аспекте.

cases.sentence: Я не дурак, я понимаю, есть еще на свете ___.
cases.translation: I am no fool, I understand that there is still psychiatry in the world.
cases.explain: In the existential construction «есть …» the thing that exists is the subject, so it stays in the nominative.

reading.ru: Настолько размягчаюсь, что от десятой смежаю глаза, так же неодолимо.
reading.question: What does the narrator say the tenth dose does to him?
options: It makes his eyes close irresistibly
reading.correct: It makes his eyes close irresistibly
reading.explain: He softens from the fifth dose onwards, and by the tenth his eyes shut of their own accord.

reading.question: What was the result of forcing himself past his drowsiness to drink an eleventh dose?
options: No return of the growing-stronger effect at all
A second, stronger wave of manliness
reading.correct: No return of the growing-stronger effect at all
reading.explain: He had hoped for a relapse of the 'coming of age' effect, but says he tried it and there were none.

reading.ru: Я бился над этой загадкой три года подряд, ежедневно бился, и все-таки ежедневно после десятой засыпал.
reading.question: How long did the narrator wrestle with this puzzle?
options: Three years in a row, every single day
reading.correct: Three years in a row, every single day
reading.explain: He says he fought with it daily for three years and still fell asleep after the tenth dose every time.

reading.ru: А ведь все раскрылось так просто!
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the solution once he finally found it?
options: It turned out to be perfectly simple
It came to him from a doctor
reading.correct: It turned out to be perfectly simple
reading.explain: He introduces his discovery by exclaiming that everything turned out so simply.

reading.ru: Другими словами, вам надо одним волевым усилием, одним махом – не выпить ни шестой, ни седьмой, ни восьмой, ни девятой.
reading.question: What does his method actually require you to do with doses six through nine?
options: Not drink them at all — drink them only in the imagination
Drink all four of them in one gulp
reading.correct: Not drink them at all — drink them only in the imagination
reading.explain: The trick is to drink the sixth to ninth 'ideally', that is only in imagination, and so to skip them by one act of will.

reading.ru: Нет, честное слово, я презираю поколение, идущее вслед за нами.
reading.question: How does the narrator feel about the generation coming after his own?
options: He hopes it will do better
reading.explain: He states flatly that he despises the generation following his own, and that it inspires disgust and horror in him.

reading.ru: Максим Горький песен о них не споет, нечего и думать.
reading.question: What does the narrator say about Maxim Gorky and the younger generation?
options: Gorky will never sing songs about them
Gorky already wrote a book about them
Gorky drank exactly as they do
reading.correct: Gorky will never sing songs about them
reading.explain: He dismisses the idea that Gorky, the singer of heroes, could ever celebrate this generation.

reading.ru: А вот им – на все наплевать.
reading.question: What contrast does the narrator draw between his generation and the next one?
options: His own generation still cared about many things, while the young ones care about nothing
His own generation had far more sacred things
The young ones drink far less than he did
The young ones work much harder than he did
reading.correct: His own generation still cared about many things, while the young ones care about nothing
reading.explain: He admits they had very few sacred things, but plenty of things they did not shrug off — unlike the young.

reading.ru: В первый день вы к полуночи становитесь как одержимый.
reading.question: In his thought experiment, what are you like by midnight after a day of nothing but white vodka?
reading.explain: A day of white vodka leaves you possessed and blazing by midnight.

reading.ru: Вы, как костер, – сидите, а они через вас прыгают.
reading.question: What does the white-vodka drinker become on Ivan Kupala night?
options: A bonfire the girls jump over
A river the girls wade through
A tree the girls dance around
A guard who chases the girls away
reading.correct: A bonfire the girls jump over
reading.explain: He pictures himself sitting like a midsummer bonfire while the girls leap over him.

reading.ru: А если вы с утра до ночи пили только крепленые красные вина?
reading.question: What happens instead if you spend the day drinking only fortified red wine?
options: The girls will not jump over you, and you cannot even jump over a seated girl
The girls jump over you twice as eagerly
reading.correct: The girls will not jump over you, and you cannot even jump over a seated girl
reading.explain: Red wine reverses the picture: no one jumps over you, and you cannot manage to jump over a girl sitting down.

reading.question: Which narrowly specialised field of research does the narrator propose?
reading.explain: He offers drunken hiccups, studied in their mathematical aspect, as the promising field.

reading.ru: Мой глупый земляк Солоухин зовет вас в лес соленые рыжики собирать.
reading.question: What does the narrator's fellow countryman Soloukhin invite people to do?
options: Go into the forest to gather salted mushrooms
reading.correct: Go into the forest to gather salted mushrooms
reading.explain: He mocks Soloukhin's invitation to gather salted saffron milk caps and tells the reader to spit on them.

reading.ru: Лучше оставьте янкам внегалактическую астрономию, а немцам – психиатрию.
reading.question: Which peoples does the narrator say should be left astronomy and psychiatry?
options: Extragalactic astronomy to the Yankees, psychiatry to the Germans
Extragalactic astronomy to the Germans, psychiatry to the Yankees
Both of them to the Italians
Both of them to the Spaniards
reading.correct: Extragalactic astronomy to the Yankees, psychiatry to the Germans
reading.explain: He hands each foreign nation its own pursuit and keeps hiccups for 'us'.

reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: With the declaration that 'we' will take up hiccups
With the train arriving at Kupavna
With a toast to Maxim Gorky
reading.correct: With the declaration that 'we' will take up hiccups
reading.explain: After parcelling out astronomy, psychiatry, bullfighting and bel canto to others, he repeats that hiccups are our calling.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that the sixth to the ninth doses should be drunk 'ideally', that is only in the imagination?
sentences: А ведь все раскрылось так просто!
Оказывается, если вы уже выпили пятую, вам надо и шестую, и седьмую, и восьмую, и девятую выпить сразу, одним махом – но выпить идеально, то есть выпить только в воображении.
Другими словами, вам надо одним волевым усилием, одним махом – не выпить ни шестой, ни седьмой, ни восьмой, ни девятой.
highlight.explain: Only the second sentence contains the idea of drinking them in imagination; the third restates it as simply not drinking them.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the two feelings the younger generation stirs in the narrator?
sentences: Нет, честное слово, я презираю поколение, идущее вслед за нами.
Оно внушает мне отвращение и ужас.
Максим Горький песен о них не споет, нечего и думать.
Я не говорю, что мы в их годы волокли с собою целый груз святынь.
Боже упаси! – святынь у нас было совсем чуть-чуть, но зато сколько вещей, на которые нам было не наплевать.
А вот им – на все наплевать.
highlight.explain: The second sentence gives the two feelings by name: disgust and horror.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what a red-wine drinker fails to do when a girl sits down on Ivan Kupala night?
sentences: А если вы с утра до ночи пили только крепленые красные вина?
Да девушки через вас и прыгать не станут в ночь на Ивана Купала.
Даже наоборот: сядет девушка в ночь на Ивана Купала, а вы через нее и перепрыгнуть не сумеете, не то что другое чего.
Конечно, при условии, что вы с утра до вечера пили только красное!..
highlight.explain: The third sentence reverses the picture: he cannot even jump over a girl who has sat down.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what the narrator's fellow countryman calls people into the forest to do?
sentences: Да, да!
А сколько захватывающего сулят эксперименты в узкоспециальных областях!
Ну, например, икота.
Мой глупый земляк Солоухин зовет вас в лес соленые рыжики собирать.
Да плюньте вы ему в его соленые рыжики!
Давайте лучше займитесь икотой, то есть исследованием пьяной икоты в ее математическом аспекте…
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence is the one that reports Soloukhin's invitation to gather salted mushrooms.

highlight.question: Which sentence contains the narrator's answer that no calling is false and every calling deserves respect?
sentences: Но ведь все это – не наше, все это нам навязали Петр Великий и Николай Кибальчич, а ведь наше призвание совсем не здесь, наше призвание совсем в другой стороне!
В той самой стороне, куда я вас приведу, если вы не станете упираться.
Вы скажете: «Призвание это гнусно и ложно».
А я вам скажу, я вам снова повторю: «Нет ложных призваний, надо уважать всякое призвание».
highlight.explain: The last sentence is his reply to the objection quoted just before it.

highlight.question: Which sentence hands astronomy and psychiatry over to other nations?
sentences: И тьфу на вас, наконец!
Лучше оставьте янкам внегалактическую астрономию, а немцам – психиатрию.

Пусть всякая сволота вроде испанцев идет на свою корриду глядеть, пусть подлец-африканец строит свою Асуанскую плотину, пусть строит, подлец, все равно ее ветром сдует, пусть подавится Италия своим дурацким бельканто, пусть!..
highlight.explain: The second sentence assigns extragalactic astronomy to the Yankees and psychiatry to the Germans.
